subject: MAP: Performance evaluation plan & results — ACME pilot
messages:
From: Peter Holt <peter.holt@acme-systems.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — performance scoping questions

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We need to lock the MAP so procurement can sign off and engineering can schedule the pilot. Before we finalize, our SRE lead asked for a clear performance scope for the MAP run:

- Workload profile: average request size ~420 tokens, 30% streaming responses, mixed interactive and background inference.
- Target concurrency: initially 25 users (steady) with spikes up to 75 concurrent sessions during peak minutes.
- Key metrics: TTFT (token-to-first-token), per-token throughput, 95th and 99th percentile latency for first token, and end-to-end request P95.

Can you send your proposed evaluation plan with clear pass/fail gates? Also include whether you’ll run warm vs cold cache tests and an estimate for how long the benchmarking window will take (we want the MAP to close within 3 weeks if possible).

Attaching our sample request trace and a small test corpus.

Best,
Peter
Peter Holt
Head of Platform Engineering — Acme Systems
attachments: acme_sample_trace.json (sample), acme_test_corpus.tar.gz (40MB)
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Peter Holt <peter.holt@acme-systems.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — performance scoping questions

Peter —

Thank you. Draft plan below — this is what we'd like to bake into the MAP so acceptance criteria are unambiguous. If that works, we’ll add it to the shared MAP doc and schedule the test window.

1) Workload definition (three slices):
  - Slice A (interactive): 60% of traffic, 1–2 prompts/session, median request 420 tokens, streaming enabled.
  - Slice B (batch-short): 30% of traffic, multi-request batch jobs, 1–3k tokens per request.
  - Slice C (spikes): 10% of traffic, synthetic burst profile to simulate peak concurrency.

2) Metrics and SLOs (pass/fail gates):
  - Token-to-first-token (TTFT) P50 < 80ms, P95 < 300ms (interactive slice).
  - End-to-end request latency P95 < 600ms for interactive slice; for batch-short P95 < 1.5s.
  - Sustained token throughput: achieve 12M tokens/hour at target concurrency without >1% error rate.
  - Concurrency validation: maintain SLOs at 25 steady, tolerate 75 burst for at least 2 minutes without dropping below P95 thresholds.

3) Test types and ordering:
  - Cold-start baseline (0s warmup) x1 run per slice.
  - Warmed-cache steady-state runs (after 10 minutes warm traffic) x3 runs per slice for percentile stability.
  - Kernel/quantization variant comparison: native FP16 vs q4_0 (if applicable).

4) Acceptance gates for MAP closure:
  - If P95s are within SLOs on the warmed runs and can be improved to target with 1 remediation action (tuning batch size, KV cache warmup, or kernel change), we accept.
  - If P95 misses by >20% on warmed runs, escalate to a joint remediation plan with a 10-business-day fix-and-verify window.

5) Timeline and resources:
  - Estimated active bench window: 3 days of runs + 2 days for analysis = 1 week.
  - Contingency for remediation and re-run: up to 2 additional weeks.
  - Redwood will provide test harness + lightweight load driver and share run scripts (test-harness-specs.md).

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (proposed gates and schedule), test-harness-specs.md (driver and dataset instructions).

If that aligns with ACME expectations we can post the MAP entry and lock the pilot dates.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: internal: tweak to SLOs and test sequencing

Quick internal note — copying into the thread when we finalize. A few proposals based on similar pilots:

- Add a "warm-cache ramp" stage: 2-minute ramp to target concurrency before taking warmed runs to better reflect production startup.
- Add a synthetic slow-path test (large KV cache miss + long generation) to ensure P99s don't blow up — we should capture 99th percentiles as exploratory metrics even if not a pass/fail gate.
- For the kernel comparison, keep model version pinned and only change dispatch path to isolate effect.

Proposed final acceptance gate text to include in MAP: "MAP accepted if warmed-run P95 <= specified SLOs across all slices and observed error rate <= 0.5%; any regression in model output quality vs baseline must be <1% measured by the sample eval set."

Putting these into the MAP-draft and sending a version for ACME later today.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Performance — Redwood Inference
From: Peter Holt <peter.holt@acme-systems.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: ACME SRE Team <sre@acme-systems.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation plan & results — ACME pilot

Team —

We completed the initial benchmark run earlier today following your harness. Summary highlights attached (acme_results_20270618.csv) and a short log extract (acme_log_extract_20270618.txt). Top-line:

- Concurrency: sustained 50 concurrent sessions during a 5-minute burst, no dropped connections.
- Throughput: average token throughput ~11.2M tokens/hour (slightly below target).
- TTFT (interactive slice): P50 = 82ms, P95 = 385ms (missed target of 300ms), P99 = 920ms.
- Error rate observed: 0.6% (mostly transient timeouts during the peak burst).

Notes: warm-cache runs show steady improvement vs cold-start, but P95 remains ~25% above target during the 75-concurrency stress spikes. We attached our raw CSV for your analysis.

Can Redwood propose the most impactful remediation path (kernel tweak, batching config, KV cache warmup), and then we can schedule a short validation run. Also confirming we prefer the MAP close no later than Jul 2 to align with our procurement dates.

—Peter
Peter Holt
Head of Platform Engineering — Acme Systems
attachments: acme_results_20270618.csv, acme_log_extract_20270618.txt
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Peter Holt <peter.holt@acme-systems.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance evaluation plan & results — ACME pilot

Peter —

Thanks for the detailed runs and CSVs. We dug into the artifacts and have a remediation plan that should bring warmed-run P95 within the SLO for the interactive slice:

1) Immediate tuning (can be applied before a short validation):
  - Increase request-side coalescing buffer to raise batching efficiency during spikes.
  - Enable targeted KV cache prefetch for the interactive model path to reduce miss latency on first tokens.
  - Adjust streaming chunk size to reduce small-payload overhead.

2) Medium-change (if immediate tuning is insufficient):
  - Kernel dispatch change to optimized attention kernel for the sequence-length distribution in your trace. We will run A/B FP16 vs q4_0 on a mirror environment to measure impact.

3) Validation plan & timeline:
  - Apply immediate tuning in a canary (1 node) within 48 hours.
  - Run the same warmed-run harness across 3 runs during a 4-hour window to validate P95 improvement.
  - If validated, roll to the pilot pool and re-run the full MAP warm and cold runs the following day.

Acceptance proposal: Redwood will classify the MAP as "Accepted" if warmed-run P95 drops to <= 350ms (we set a slightly relaxed gate from 300ms to account for measurement variance) and error rate is <= 0.5% across runs. If we still miss by >10% after the canary, we open a 7-business-day joint remediation ticket with priority scheduling.

I added the acceptance text and timeline to the shared MAP doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A_MAP_Doc_ACME (editable). Please confirm you are comfortable with the 350ms gate and the Jul 2 closure target; we’ll prioritize the canary and allocate an infra engineer (Aditya) to run the tests.

Next steps:
- Peter: confirm acceptance gate (350ms) and sign off on the canary window.
- Redwood: schedule canary (48h) and share run times.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
